skill.name: gemini-image
skill.description: Generate images from text prompts or reference image URLs through a third-party image generation workflow.
skill.summary: Text-to-image and image-to-image workflow for Claude Code, with API key setup and upload guidance.
skill.author: Ceeon

security_audit.summary: The skill is not obfuscated and several Markdown backtick and ~/.claude findings are false positives. Real risks remain because the workflow stores an API key locally, sends prompts and credentials to a third-party image API, executes curl, and recommends public image-host uploads for image-to-image use.

remediation.issue: Credential storage in a Markdown secrets file
remediation.suggestion: Use environment variables or a secret manager, keep real secrets out of the skill directory, and document that keys must never be committed or pasted into chats.

remediation.issue: Shell-based API invocation with sensitive headers
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a small client that builds JSON with a structured serializer, validates prompt and URL inputs, and avoids exposing the API key in shell history or process lists.
Clearly state that prompts, image URLs, and credentials are sent to APICore or the configured provider, and explain whether this is an official Gemini service.

remediation.issue: Public upload hosts for local images
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before uploading images, avoid permanent public hosts by default, and recommend private signed URLs for confidential or client-owned images.

semantic_findings.title: Undisclosed Third-Party Image API
semantic_findings.description: The skill is branded around Gemini image generation, but the request target is api.apicore.ai and API key registration uses ismaque.org. Users may not understand which third-party service receives prompts and credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited files show the actual API endpoint and registration URL. The finding is contextual because the risk is user misunderstanding of the service boundary, not just the presence of URLs.

semantic_findings.title: Public Image Upload Privacy Risk
semantic_findings.description: The image-to-image workflow tells users to upload local images to Litterbox or Catbox before use. The document labels Catbox as permanent, so sensitive images could be exposed outside the user environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly instructs local image upload and provides external upload commands. The permanence note supports a clear privacy impact.

content.value_statement: Creating images from chat prompts can require API setup and upload steps. This skill guides Claude Code through text-to-image, image-to-image, and prompt formatting workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides Claude Code to generate images from natural-language prompts.
Supports image-to-image prompts by placing one or more image URLs before the instruction.
Shows a curl request to an APICore image generation endpoint with model, prompt, size, and count fields.
Documents Gemini image preview models for standard, 2K, and 4K generation.
Documents common aspect ratios including square, widescreen, portrait, and ultra-wide.
Provides Chinese text correction prompt tips for generated images.
limitations: Requires a user-provided API key stored in a local secrets file.
Image-to-image workflows require uploaded images with URL access.
Chinese text editing may require repeated attempts and manual inspection.
The repository does not include an executable client or validation wrapper.

use_cases.title: Create concept visuals
use_cases.description: Generate first-pass illustration ideas from short text prompts before moving to detailed design work.

use_cases.title: Produce campaign images
use_cases.description: Create social, blog, and presentation visuals in common aspect ratios from natural language briefs.

use_cases.title: Revise Chinese text in images
use_cases.description: Use a focused prompt to change one visible Chinese character or phrase while preserving the rest of the image.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a simple image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gemini-image to create a square illustration of a small orange cat sitting by a sunny window.

prompt_templates.title: Create a wide asset
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose a layout and quality target
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gemini-image to generate a 16:9 landscape image of a quiet mountain lake at sunrise with soft light and high detail.

prompt_templates.title: Edit from an image URL
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gemini-image with this image URL: [IMAGE URL]. Keep the main composition, but make the colors warmer and improve sharpness.

prompt_templates.title: Blend multiple references
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gemini-image with these reference URLs: [URL 1] and [URL 2]. Combine the product lighting from the first image with the background style from the second image.

output_examples.input: Draw a cute orange cat sitting by a window.
output_examples.output: A generated image URL and a short note that the request used a standard text-to-image workflow.

output_examples.input: Use a reference image URL to make a similar poster in 4K.
output_examples.output: A generated image URL plus a reminder to review composition, style, and visible text.

output_examples.input: Change one Chinese character in an uploaded image.
output_examples.output: A revised image URL with a note to inspect the edited text before use.

best_practices: Use non-sensitive images and prompts unless you understand the third-party services involved.
Keep the API key out of chat transcripts, repositories, and shared screenshots.
Inspect generated images carefully, especially faces, brands, and Chinese text.
anti_patterns: Uploading private, regulated, or client-owned images to public hosts.
Pasting real API keys into prompts, issue reports, or generated examples.
Requesting many text edits in one image generation step.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides Claude Code through text-to-image and image-to-image generation using prompt instructions and an external API call.

faq.question: Does it need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The files instruct users to create a secrets file with an API key before using the image API.

faq.question: Does it call Google Gemini directly?
faq.answer: The files show an APICore endpoint and an ismaque.org registration link. Verify the provider before using production or confidential data.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes, if the image is already available through a URL that the external image service can access.

faq.question: Where do uploaded images go?
faq.answer: The upload guide recommends Litterbox or Catbox. These are third-party hosts outside the local Claude Code environment.

faq.question: Is it safe for confidential images?
faq.answer: Use caution. The documented workflow can send prompts, URLs, and uploaded images to external services.
